entry_points.summary: sha256 of sorted, newline-joined [x] task-ids from TASKS.md; empty set hashes ''; order-independent; the single shared hash function used by both the curator (writer) and E1 (reader) — DRY contract for resume.
Prints the id of the last [x] heading in TASKS.md; human hint only, not load-bearing for resume.
Prints the first [ ] task id whose deps are all [x]; dep-gated; human hint only.
Prints the ts of the most recent context_curated event in events_file; prints 'none' if absent. Used by E3 to compute since_marker for the next curation delta.
Prints a scalar YAML frontmatter field from SESSION.md (or empty if absent). Used by E1 to read done_ids_hash, schema_version, next_pending, last_gate_task_id cheaply without loading the body.

Haiku subagent (model: haiku); dispatched synchronously at the compaction breakpoint; folds events delta + git diff + TASKS.md + prior SESSION.md into a bounded SESSION.md; never edits production code.
Required prompt fields: plan_dir, run_id, repo_root, last_gate_task_id, tasks_file, event_source ($ZH_BASE/metrics.jsonl), slug, since_marker.

8-step ordered behavior: read prior SESSION.md; read metrics.jsonl delta backward from EOF (O(delta), not O(total)); read TASKS.md + git diff --stat; fold into 4 capped sections with overflow rule; compute metadata via helpers; atomic write; emit context_curated; return STATUS line.
Computes done_ids_hash by calling bash scripts/session-helpers.sh done_set_hash — must NOT re-implement inline. Writer and reader must produce byte-identical hashes or resume silently never fires.

Key invariants: never touches non-SESSION.md files; incremental O(delta) read; done_ids_hash always via shared helper; idempotent under retry via atomic rename; diff_unavailable on git error (never hard-fail).

On persistent failure: write frontmatter-only stub with done_ids_hash from done_set_hash helper (event-independent), overflow: true, empty sections. Stub's resume key is always valid even when event read failed.

After TASKS.md read, before first dispatch: compute CUR_HASH via done_set_hash; read SESSION.md frontmatter; use SESSION.md iff schema_version supported AND done_ids_hash==CUR_HASH AND pending remain; inline body via explicit Read; emit session_resumed. Else emit session_resume_skipped {reason}.
Emits session_resumed {done_ids_hash, last_gate_task_id, next_pending} when E1 predicate matches and SESSION.md body is inlined.
Emits session_resume_skipped {reason} on any E1 skip; reason in {no_file, done_set_mismatch, no_pending, schema_version}. On done_set_mismatch, surfaces a one-line user note.
Z_SESSION_CURATOR_TIMEOUT_S (default 120; 0 disables curator) and Z_SESSION_MAX_CHARS (default 28000) are the two env knobs for session-handoff. Defined here as the canonical reference.

After compaction_pause emit, before push-notify: dispatch context-curator synchronously with Z_SESSION_CURATOR_TIMEOUT_S. One inline retry at 2x timeout. On success emit '/clear & resume'; on persistent failure emit context_curation_failed + /compact notice; exit 0 always.

After a task hits [x]: emit context_breadcrumb {task, intent} ONLY when a concrete trigger held (decision/override, task_halt, shortcut/spec-deviation, reviewer retry). Clean completions emit nothing — keeps curator mining high-signal.
Telemetry table row for context_breadcrumb; fields: task, intent (decision_gate|task_halt_recovered|spec_deviation|reviewer_retry).

invariants: done_ids_hash is always computed via scripts/session-helpers.sh done_set_hash — never inline; writer and reader use the same helper to guarantee byte-identical hashes.
The '/clear & resume' notice fires ONLY when context-curator returned STATUS: curated AND the curator's done_ids_hash matches the current TASKS.md done-set.
context-curator never touches files other than SESSION.md (+ its .tmp.<PID> staging file). Never edits TASKS.md, SPEC.md, PLAN.md, or any production code.

Curator reads event_source ($ZH_BASE/metrics.jsonl) — not the per-plan events.jsonl or orchestration-only events.jsonl — because only metrics.jsonl aggregates both task-tier and orchestration-tier events.
Curator reads events backward from EOF, stopping at ts <= since_marker (O(delta), not O(total log)).
SESSION.md is written atomically via tmp+rename; a partial prior write is overwritten cleanly on retry.
E1 resume predicate is set-based and position-independent: same [x] set in any TASKS.md line order → same hash → resume fires. Any change to the [x] set → hash mismatch → safe skip.
Z_SESSION_CURATOR_TIMEOUT_S=0 disables the curator; behavior identical to pre-handoff (no SESSION.md written, no '/clear & resume' notice).
All [x] detection in session-helpers.sh uses the orchestrator's canonical pattern ^\s*[-*]?\s*\[x\] — no divergence.
Failure-stub path writes a valid done_ids_hash from TASKS.md directly (event-independent) so the stub's resume key is valid even when the event read failed.
session-helpers.sh functions are stdout-only, no side effects, exit 0 always (empty output = not found).
context_curated event is emitted with label 'orchestration' so the next curation's since_marker lookup finds it in metrics.jsonl.
gotchas: Re-implementing done_set_hash inline in the curator or any other caller breaks the DRY contract: the writer and reader will produce different hashes and resume will silently never fire.
Reading the per-plan events.jsonl or orchestration-only events.jsonl instead of metrics.jsonl makes the landmine backstop inert — task-tier events only appear in metrics.jsonl.
The '/clear & resume' notice must NOT be emitted until AFTER curation succeeds and the done-set hash matches. Emitting it before curation is a security-of-resume contract violation.
done_set_mismatch on E1 resume means TASKS.md was modified between the pause and the resume (e.g. a task marked [x] offline). SESSION.md is NOT inlined — the user sees a one-line note.
schema_version mismatch on E1 triggers session_resume_skipped {reason: schema_version} — the orchestrator must never attempt to parse an unknown schema.
Z_SESSION_CURATOR_TIMEOUT_S=0 disables the whole subsystem. Callers testing resume behavior must set this to a positive value.
Overflow order matters: apply entry caps FIRST, then collapse resolved decisions, then drop oldest entries if still over ceiling. Applying in a different order changes which entries are preserved.
context_curated must be emitted AFTER the atomic rename succeeds (not before); otherwise a crash between write and event leaves metrics.jsonl with a stale since_marker.
The failure-stub SESSION.md has overflow: true and empty sections; E1 will still resume from the stub (the done_ids_hash is valid), but the body inlining provides no useful context.
git diff --stat only — never capture full hunks; full hunks can be arbitrarily large and would blow the SESSION.md ceiling immediately.
